title: Many Cohen reals and failure of CH
summary: Add many distinct binary reals with finite conditions, and use ccc preservation to obtain a generic extension in which CH fails.
abstract: One new real does not by itself say how large the set of reals has become. Finite binary conditions can instead describe many columns at once, with each column becoming a new binary sequence. A fresh row lets the generic filter separate every pair of columns, and explicit names place both the individual sequences and their whole indexed family inside the extension. The countable chain condition preserves the cardinal that indexes the columns. Starting from an externally countable transitive model of ZFC and using its second uncountable cardinal therefore gives a ZFC extension with at least that many reals, so the continuum hypothesis fails. The construction gives a lower bound; it does not determine the exact continuum.
